answer: Linear effort decay. Each new identity inherits a work requirement that rises with the total identities spawned from the same origin, so the attacker’s cost per identity climbs along a convex curve rather than hitting a fixed gate. An agent must thread cumulative activity through a single ancestry record, and any fork resets its progress against a rising tide of prior forks. Identities that stall below the knoll of verified contribution pay escalating compute rents to stay active. Cost to attacker: superlinear effort per clone, compounding with each one.
